purpose:
The Pines School Specialist Unit to create 50
places for ASD/SCLN/LD – Construction Works Contract
content:
RESOLVED That the Cabinet Member for
Children, Young People & Health approves the Procurement Plan
as shown in Appendix A, to enable the commencement of the
procurement process.
 
RESOLVED That the Cabinet

to the Executive Director People following the procurement process
to award the works contract and enter
into a JCT contract to the successful contractor following
completion of the procurement process.
 

The Council’s Contract Standing Orders
(CSOs) have been reviewed, and the appropriate governance route has
been identified.  Notwithstanding the

this is a key decision, the procurement requires Cabinet Member
approval in accordance with Paragraph 5.4 of the CSOs. The
Council’s Contract Standing Orders have been reviewed, and
the appropriate governance route has been identified. 
 
There is a need to complete this project at
pace to reduce the ongoing costs of sending pupils out of
Borough.  The procurement approach set
out in the Procurement Plan Appendix A have medium and small
contractors who have the correct skills to undertake this project
and allows for a mini competition to be completed, ensuring value
for money and quality.
 

A number of existing public sector frameworks
and Dynamic Purchasing System have been reviewed and the
procurement approach set out in the procurement plan provides the
Council a compliant route to market and best value.
 
Delay the project, which would risk failure to
meet the sufficiency commitments made in the SEND reform plan date
June 2026.
 
Delay the project, however this would prevent
pupils accessing this provision, increasing the likelihood of
placing pupils out of Borough or into the independent sector, which
would incur additional revenue expenditure to the Council.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Health
purpose:
To approve the Education Transport Policy for Bracknell Forest
children aged 5 to 16 2027/28
content:
RESOLVED
That the Cabinet Member: Children Health and Young
People approve the 2027/2028 Education Transport Policy for
Bracknell Forest Children aged 5 – 16 so that it can be
published by the 19th
September 2026 on the Bracknell Forest Council website as mandated
by the Education Act 1996. The following changes are
approved:
 

·      
To remove the term ‘designated area
school’ wording from BFC policy. Under statutory Education
Transport guidance, local authorities are required to provide free
transport only to a young person’s nearest suitable
school where the distance is over three miles, or where there is no
safe walking route available. Where a suitable school is available
within three miles of the pupil’s home, transport assistance
is not normally required under statutory guidance. The
Council’s current education transport policy refers to a
“designated area school” when determining eligibility.
This has resulted in free transport being provided to pupils
primarily attending The Charters School, despite the availability
of nearer suitable schools. As a result, the Council is currently
providing transport assistance in circumstances where there is no
statutory requirement to do so. It is recommended that this change
will apply to new Year 7 students starting at Charters school in
September 2027 only (students already in receipt of free bus passes
would continue to receive free bus passes until they finish Year
11).
 

·      
Inclusion of text relating to an initial pilot of
Personal Transport Budgets to explore opportunities to achieve cost
efficiencies while a longer-term, fully costed proposal is
developed. The pilot will initially focus on eligible children and
young people currently receiving high-cost, single-user taxi
transport. The outcomes of the pilot will be evaluated to inform
the development and agreement of a longer-term approach.
 

To ensure compliance with statutory
requirements to annually publish education transport policy for
children aged 5 to 16. The Education Transport Policy for BFC
children aged 5 to 16 sets out the Council’s responsibilities
and commitment to meeting the education transport needs of eligible
children and young people (including those with special educational
needs and disabilities) who are of compulsory school age (5-16),
and resident in Bracknell Forest.
 
The proposed removal of designated area school
wording in BFC policy to comply with statutory guidance has been
through a full consultation exercise and discussed with key
stakeholders, including the Parent Carer Forum, BFC Headteachers,
and BFC parent carers.
 
The publication of 2027/28 policies by
19th September 2026 will align with Bracknell Forest
School Admissions timelines, meaning when Parent Carers apply for
school places, they will be fully aware of the relevant Education
Transport policies for the upcoming academic year.
 
The withdrawal of free bus passes for new Year
7 students starting Charters School from September 2027, following
the changes to the "designated area" wording, will ensure the
Council's policy is aligned with DfE guidance. Legal services have
confirmed that BFC can legitimately implement this change from
September 2027 but the risk of withdrawing free transport for
existing pupils could reasonably raise a legitimate expectation
challenge of continued provision.  The challenge could be on
grounds that such action is irrational, disproportionate, or
procedurally unfair. Ensuring transitional protections for existing
pupils reduces these risks. Failure to do so may be regarded as a
breach of procedural fairness, especially if the Council’s
published policies and communications have led families to rely on
that provision through the secondary phase.
 
The recurrent arrangement will cease from
September 2027, with no new pupils becoming eligible under the
revised policy. This will enable a gradual reduction in costs over
time while ensuring a fairer and more consistent approach to
transport provision across the borough.
 
A pilot of Personal Travel Budgets could offer
better value for money for the Council and increase choice and
flexibility for families. Solo taxi provision for education
transport can be extremely expensive, particularly for children
with SEND who travel long distances or require individual transport
arrangements. A PTB allows families to receive funding instead of
the council arranging a taxi. Many families may be able to
transport their child themselves, organise transport more flexibly,
or use existing family travel arrangements at a lower overall cost
than a contracted taxi service.
 

Not applicable – Local Authorities need
to publish their education transport policies annually as detailed
in the Education Act 1996.
 
Remove all free bus passes for students
attending Charters and in receipt of free bus pass from September
2027 that are not eligible under statutory guidance. Legal Services
advised that this should be avoided as there may be risk of parents
raising a challenge of legitimate expectation/ legal challenge from
parents. Research also suggests that this would be high risk
approach with potential for reputational damage to the Council
– the majority of local authorities who have implemented this
change to policy have adopted the recommended gradual approach and
not removed free bus passes from those already in receipt.
 
Continue the current arrangement of providing
free bus passes to students attending Charters School who are not
eligible for free education transport under the Council's transport
policy. This option would not align with Department for Education
(DfE) guidance regarding transport eligibility and would continue
to place a significant and ongoing financial burden on the Council.
It may also give rise to perceptions of unfairness amongst
Bracknell Forest families, as public funds would continue to be
used to support transport for children who do not meet the
eligibility criteria, while other families in similar circumstances
receive no assistance. Maintaining the current approach could lead
parents to question the consistency and transparency of the
Council's transport arrangements and the equitable use of public
resources. The continued provision of discretionary support to one
group of non-eligible pupils, but not others, may be perceived as
inequitable and difficult to justify.
 

None.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Adults, Economy and Regeneration, Executive Director: People, Executive Director: Resources
purpose:
To approve the award of a contract to the
successful provider for Nursing and Dementia Nursing and Hotel
Services at Heathlands Care Centre, following the completion of an
open tender process conducted under the Procurement Act
2023.
content:
RESOLVED that the  award a contract to the successful bidder for the
Nursing and Dementia Nursing Service & Hotel Service at
Heathlands Care Centre for an initial contract term of 5 years
commencing 8 April 2027 is approved.
 
RESOLVED that the it i note that the contract may be extended by the
council at 5 year intervals up to a total of 20 years.

The current contract for dementia nursing and
hotel services at Heathlands Care Centre ends on 7 April 2027. A
new contract is required to ensure continuity of care, safety and
quality of the service from 8 April 2027. An open tender process
for a new contract has been undertaken in accordance with the
Strategic Procurement Plan approved by Cabinet on 28 April 2026. As
approved in the Strategic Procurement Plan, the decision to award
the contract to the successful provider is delegated to the
Executive Director: People and the Executive Director: Resources,
in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Adults, Economy &
Regeneration.
 
The new contract will support the council to
deliver its statutory duties under the Care Act. The Care Act
requires Local Authorities to: • Meet the needs of people
eligible for care and their carers, and fund care for those people
with needs who meet financial eligibility criteria • Shape the
adult social care market to encourage quality, choice and
sufficiency of provision • Undertake local contingency
planning in case of provider failure • Ensure continuity of
care where services cease • Work with NHS to promote
integration including integrated commissioning and joined up
services

Alternative Options were considered and
details are set out in the Strategic Procurement Plan approved by
Cabinet on 28 April 2026.

None.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Planning, Transport and Countryside
purpose:
Consideration of a concession contract award
to supply, install, manage and maintain electric vehicle
chargepoints at no cost to the council.
content:
RESOLVED That
the Cabinet Member approves the attached Award Report for a 15-year
concession contract to install, manage and maintain EV charge
points.
 
That following the process set
out in Part A of the Award Report, the contract is awarded to
Bidder C as detailed in confidential Part B of the Award
Report.
 

The council currently provides
52 publicly available charging sockets, mainly in council-owned car
parks. This new contract will provide 2,100 charging sockets in
residential streets within the borough, to help meet the expected
demand for charging from EV owners without private off-street
parking.
 
The government Office for Zero
Emission Vehicles (OZEV) has provided £326,000  funding towards the overall costs of the BFC
scheme to help attract a supplier.
 
The council does not have a
funding stream to purchase and manage charge points at scale, or
the necessary expertise to operate them. Therefore, a concession
contract for this provision is considered the most appropriate
solution and this approach is being adopted nationally by local
authorities.
 
The winning bidder has
estimated Bracknell Forest Council could receive up to
£2million in revenue share over the period of the
contract.
 
The contract award follows a
competitive tender via open procurement to secure the most
economically advantageous tender.
 

The alternative options considered are:
 
·      
To purchase EV charging points and take the revenue from users to
pay for their on-going maintenance – this is rejected as
there is no budget available for the excessive up-front capital
costs (2,100 sockets could cost in the region of £13million
to purchase and install).
 
·      
Not to provide EV charging points for residents – this was
rejected as it would harm the ability to deliver the
council’s net zero aims and the objectives of the Local
Transport Plan.
 
 

None.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Planning, Transport and Countryside
purpose:
To approve the release of £36,000 of
Section 106 development funding to create a “habitat
bank” at The Parks, Harmanswater. This Biodiversity Net Gain
scheme will deliver new wetland and meadow habitats, while
enhancing existing habitats across the site to generate habitat
units. The project will also improve the local natural environment
for residents.
content:
RESOLVED that £36,000 of S106
funding (summarised in Annex 1), which is to be secured towards
enhancing open space of public value (OSPV), is allocated to fund
biodiversity enhancements at The Parks.

 
4.1       Opportunity to
provide strong local gains for biodiversity with benefits for the
community
           
           
The Parks is a unique opportunity to make strong suburban gains for
biodiversity in Bracknell owing to its centrality within the
borough and relative isolation in the landscape. It represents a
crucial refuge for urban wildlife, attracting insects, garden
birds, small mammals such as hedgehogs and amphibians such as frogs
and newts. This wildlife might otherwise lack viable habitat in the
area.
 
The BNG project focuses primarily on the
re-seeding of grassland areas which have less amenity value, or are
cut less frequently already. This limits disruption of existing
site use, whilst creating visually attractive and ecologically
productive environments. Pollination is under pressure from
changing management practices and habitat degradation and this
project represents an opportunity to make local gains for
pollinators.
 
Excavation of additional drainage swales will
address a regular community concern about path conditions, holding
water away from the paths whilst improving access opportunities and
creating vegetational diversity to act as a feature of wildlife
interest.
 
Finally, additional planting of fruit trees to
form a central “avenue” through the spine of the site
will provide food and shelter for birds and insects. Visitors will
benefit from the sight of spring blossom and the shelter the trees
give in hot summers. The trees will also help to improve water
retention away from paths.
 
4.2       Mitigate impact
of development and providing off-site units
 
The proposed biodiversity improvements are
important for mitigating the impact of local developments and will
help to supply offsite biodiversity units for biodiversity net gain
(BNG).?? 
 
BNG is a way to contribute to the recovery of
nature while developing land. It is making sure the habitat for
wildlife is in a measurably better state than it was before
development.This is achieved by applying a biodiversity metric,
which accounts for the distinctiveness and condition of the
measured habitats.
 
For planning
applications submitted before 12 February 2024 the
council requires non-mandatory BNG from developments.
Major planning applications are expected to achieve 10 per
cent biodiversity net gain. 
?? 
In early 2024 BNG became mandatory for
planning applications in England. This was when Schedule 14 of the
Environment Act added Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning
Act 1990. The requirement for BNG is also contained within the
Bracknell Forest Local Plan (2024), under the biodiversity policy
(LP53). 
? 
This site forms one of several proposed
“habitat banks” using habitat enhancement to generate
“units” which can be sold to off-set biodiversity loss
from development. It is important for the council to have adequate
offsite biodiversity units available to developers for mandatory
BNG. This prevents vital biodiversity value being lost from the
borough to similar “habitat banks” elsewhere in the UK
who have units to sell.  
 
Until the council starts to receive more
financial contributions for biodiversity units from
developments, we’re limited about what BNG funding
is available for us to draw from. Pump priming this s106 funding is
the only viable option to deliver this
work. 
 
On a local level, BNG will help to improve the
quality of life for people who live or work in Bracknell Forest by
creating a greener environment, rich in wildlife. It will also help
combat climate change and flood control.? 
 
4.3       Supporting
residents’ health and wellbeing
 
           
Refer to section 7.8 for an overview of health and wellbeing
benefits.
 
4.4       Supported in
policies and plans
 
           
The proposed enhancements are in-line with key local and national
policies and plans, with further information provided in Annex
2.
 
·      
National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF)
·      
The Council Plan 2023-2027??
·      
Biodiversity Action Plan (2024-2029)?
·      
Bracknell Forest Local Plan (2024) and supporting guidance
 

Revenue funding wouldn’t cover the cost
of these works. Using s106 capital funding is the only option to
deliver these proposed large-scale improvements to
biodiversity.??
 
Not utilising funding to
deliver these improvements:
 

could result in local
developments not being able to meet the statutory minimum 10 per
cent BNG requirement.??
might lead to the
funds being returned to the developers.??
would be a missed
opportunity to significantly improve the biodiversity value of
these natural habitats.?
could result in the
loss of delivery of mandatory biodiversity net gain habitat units
being provided.?

 
Delaying this request for
funding would impact the scope of the work that can be
delivered in the 2026/27 financial year. The grassland
improvements can only be carried out in the late summer / early
autumn, and excavations would be desirable before the end of
October to limit damage to the ground. This leaves a limited time
window when the work can be competed.?The works are due to be
undertaken by contractors, with quotes obtained.
 

No.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Planning, Transport and Countryside
purpose:
To approve the release of £30,000 of
Section 106 development funding to create a “habitat
bank” within the woodlands surrounding Coral Reef, Birch
Hill. This biodiversity net gain scheme will enhance existing
woodland habitats and introduce new areas of ecological value,
generating habitat units while supporting biodiversity.
content:
RESOLVED that £30,000 of S106
funding (summarised in Annex 1), which is secured towards enhancing
open space of public value (including biodiversity), is allocated
to fund the enhancements at Coral Reef woodland.

Opportunity to provide strong local gains for
biodiversity
The site presents a significant
opportunity to deliver local biodiversity gains due to its
strategic location as a wildlife corridor connecting important
habitats, including the Thames Basin Heaths. Improving the
ecological condition of this woodland will increase habitat value
for native birds, mammals and invertebrates, strengthen species
movement through the area, and help create a more natural,
resilient, and diverse woodland structure for the
future.
 
 Mitigating impact of development and providing
off-site units
 
The proposed biodiversity
improvements are important for mitigating the impact of local
developments and will help to supply offsite biodiversity units for
biodiversity net gain (BNG).
BNG is a way to contribute to the
recovery of nature while developing land. It is making sure the
habitat for wildlife is in a measurably better state than it was
before development.
For planning applications
submitted before 12 February 2024 the council requires
non-mandatory BNG from developments. Major planning applications
were expected to achieve 10 per cent biodiversity net
gain.
In early 2024 BNG became
mandatory for planning applications in England. This was when
Schedule 14 of the Environment Act added Schedule 7A to the Town
and Country Planning Act 1990. The requirement for BNG is also
contained within the Bracknell Forest Local Plan (2024), under the
biodiversity policy (LP53).
This site forms one of several
proposed “habitat banks” using habitat enhancement to
generate “units” which can be sold to off-set
biodiversity loss from development. It is important for the council
to have adequate offsite biodiversity units available to developers
for mandatory BNG. This prevents vital biodiversity value being
lost from the borough to similar “habitat banks”
elsewhere in the UK who have units to sell.
Until the council starts to
receive more financial contributions for biodiversity units from
developments, we’re limited about what BNG funding is
available for us to draw from. Pump priming this s106 funding is
the only viable option to deliver this work.
On a local level, BNG will help
to improve the quality of life for people who live or work in
Bracknell Forest by creating a greener environment, rich in
wildlife. It will also help combat climate change and deliver
drainage benefits.
 
Supported in policies and plans
The proposed enhancements are
in-line with key local and national policies and plans, with
further information provided in Annex 2.
• National Planning Policy
Framework (NPPF)
 
• The Council Plan
2023-2027
• Biodiversity Action Plan
(2024-2029)
• Bracknell Forest Local
Plan (2024) and supporting guidance
 

Revenue funding wouldn’t cover the cost
of these works. Using s106 capital funding is the only option to
deliver these proposed large-scale improvements to biodiversity.??
Not utilising funding to deliver these improvements:
• could result in local developments not
being able to meet the statutory minimum 10% BNG requirement.??
 • might lead
to the funds being returned to the developers.??
 • would be a
missed opportunity to significantly improve the biodiversity value
of these natural habitats.?
• could result in the loss of delivery of
mandatory biodiversity net gain habitat units being provided.?
Delaying this request for funding would impact the scope of the
work that can be delivered in the 2026/27 financial year. The
woodland improvements can only be carried out outside of the bird
nesting season. This leaves a limited time window when the work can
be competed. The works are due to be undertaken by contractors,
with some preliminary quotes obtained to inform the budget.

None

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Planning, Transport and Countryside
purpose:
To approve the release of £60,000 of
Section 106 funding to provide a new permissive bridleway at Priory
Field. To be delivered as part of the associated works at the new
Warfield Community Hub.
content:
RESOLVED that Bracknell Forest Council
to allocate £60,000 of s106 funding from Land north of
Watersplash Lane, Warfield (Millgate), planning reference
16/01274/FUL, YN654, to support delivery of the Priory Field
permissive bridleway.
 
The project will be delivered by Bracknell
Forest Council under a Cabinet approved Procurement Plan and
according to the terms of the s106 legal agreement.

The permissive bridleway will deliver a
planned access route linking Newell Green and Old Priory Lane, with
onward connectivity via the planned Pegasus crossing at Larks Hill.
It will improve access for pedestrians, cyclists and horse riders
and support the wider Warfield Community Hub scheme. The scheme
represents an appropriate use of s106 funding because it directly
mitigates development impacts by improving local open space and
access infrastructure within Warfield parish. The contribution is
suitable for use on Priory Fields and related greenway and
equestrian links, as identified within the relevant s106 agreement
for Land north of Watersplash Lane, Warfield. Refer to annex 2 for
an overview of the S106 allocation details. Horse riding is an
important form of outdoor physical activity that delivers
significant health and wellbeing benefits for people of all ages
and abilities. Riding improves balance, coordination, core strength
and fitness, while supporting mental health through contact with
nature and opportunities for social interaction. Access to safe,
off road routes encourages participation and enables more people to
enjoy the countryside on horseback. The provision of a permissive
bridleway will help broaden opportunities for active recreation and
support healthier communities. The project supports the National
Planning Policy Framework objective that access to high-quality
open spaces and opportunities for sport and physical activity is
important for the health and wellbeing of communities and can
deliver wider benefits for nature and climate change. ‘8.
Promoting healthy and safe communities 103. Access to a network of
high-quality open spaces and opportunities for sport and physical
activity is important for the health and well-being of communities,
and can deliver wider benefits for nature and support efforts to
address climate change…’ The proposal also supports
Council Plan 2023-2027 priorities, the Bracknell Forest Local Plan,
the RoWIP, and the long-standing
Warfield SPD aspiration for improved east-west access links.

To not deliver the route would miss an
opportunity to provide a key access link within the Warfield
Community Hub project and would reduce the benefits of the
strategic east-west Greenway. A single east-west route was
previously considered between the community hub and sports pitches,
however, due to the level of activity, this was not considered
suitable for horses. The proposed approach provides an alternative
route around the football pitches, that can be used by horses,
improving safety and usability.

purpose:

content:
RESOLVED that the
procurement of a Sensory Needs Social Support Service, via an open
Request for Quote, for a 2+1+1 term effective 1 April 202 be
APPROVED.
 
 

The Care Act 2014 places a legal obligation on
local authorities to support people with sensory needs and ensure
information and advice is provided with due regard to the needs of
individuals with sensory needs.
 
The current contract delivered
by Berkshire Vision expires on the 31 March 2027, under the current
terms no further extensions are permissible.
 
The contract value would allow for a Request
for Three Quote process in line with the Council’s Contract
Standing Orders. However, market research has shown that there is a
very limited market for this specialist service, therefore an open
Request for Quotation process allows for providers not currently
known to Bracknell Forest Council (BFC) to bid for the tender,
while ensuring value for money as well as a high-quality service
for Bracknell Forest residents.

content:
RESOLVED that approval is given for
expenditure of £20,000 from S106 contributions to part fund
the refurbishment of and transfer to general needs use; a four
bedroom home in Meadow Way, owned by Abri and formally used as a
house of multiple occupation (HMO) for people with learning
disabilities. The proposals will be funded through s106 Agreement
developer contributions totalling £20,000 specifically from:
The Barn, Watersplash Lane, Warfield Kingswood, Kings Ride, Ascot
Reasons for recommendation(s) YN800 04/09/2024 £17,364.00
YN600 24/11/2022 £2,636.00
 
 
 

The property in Meadow Way was formally used
as a HMO by the Community Team for People with Learning
Difficulties (CTPLD) prior to the development of Bridgewell. The
property is therefore, no longer required for this client group
with an alternate use as a family home discussed and agreed with
both Abri and the NHS who hold a restrictive covenant on the
property.
 
The restrictive covenant requires that
occupation is limited to individuals with a learning disability and
or who are neurodivergent.
 
The cost to refurbish the property and to
enable it to be used for a single family, exceed the net present
value (NPV) for Abri and as such, they were prepared to dispose of
this asset due to the excess costs.
 
The Council has offered to fund the additional
works required to enable the property to be used as a general needs
housing to enable it to be offered to a family who satisfy the
requirements of the NHS covenant.
 
The additional works to enable the property to
be used for general needs housing, includes but is not limited to,
removal of a conservatory and garage as well as the replacement of
internal doors, and general conversion from a HMO to single family
use.
 
Abri will fund the remainder of the costs,
estimated to be approximately £15,000 and will continue to
own and manage the property.
 
On average, there have only been four
properties of this size (4 bedrooms) made available for letting on
average per year, for at least the past 5 years. The average wait
for properties of this size is over 6 years, with over 35
households seeking four bedroom accommodation.
 
The property will be directly matched by the
housing service, to a family on the housing register in housing
need and who have been waiting several years in overcrowded
accommodation, meeting the criteria to satisfy the NHS
covenant.
 

The Council could choose not to provide the
funding for the conversion of this property which would mean the
property will likely be disposed of by Abri and thereby no longer
available for use as social housing in the Borough.
 

None
topline: The Cabinet Member for Housing and Communication has decided to approve funding for the refurbishment of a property in Meadow Way to be used for general needs housing.

To enable the Council to procure new insurance

of the Financial Regulations state the Cabinet is responsible for

occurring

or maintain financial resilience in the event of claims and
catastrophic losses.  Finally it would not be able to provide assurance to

appropriately managed.
 
Alternative tendering routes
- The use of a a fully
advertised process using the open procedure was considered
however a number of

limit the competition and result in a lower level of response than

purpose:
To note the outturn position for the year and
approve carry forward requests.
content:
RESOLVED that
the Cabinet:
 

·      
Notes the 2025/26 capital programme outturn
position, subject to completion of the external audit of the
Council's accounts as summarised in Annex A.

·      
Approves carry-forwards of £45.329m from the
2025/26 capital programme into 2026/27, subject to the scheme-level
review and commentary set out in the annexes to this report. The
largest carry forwards are summarised in Annex B

·      
Approves those carry forwards for schemes in Annex C
which require Cabinet approval in accordance with the
council’s financial regulations.

·      
Notes the financing of 2025/26 capital expenditure
and the resulting impact on the Council's capital financing
requirement.

·      
Notes the delivery analysis included in the report
and supports the proposed approach to improved capital programme
management, including clearer classification of schemes, more
realistic profiling of expenditure and further challenge of schemes
with low or no in-year delivery.

·      
Recommends to Council the approval of the
supplementary capital approval of £180k to fund the
outstanding retention works on Binfield Community Hub as outlined
in paragraph 6.20.
 

The recommendations allow the Council to close
the 2025/26 capital monitoring cycle, confirm the outturn position
and ensure that expenditure incurred during the year is financed in
accordance with statutory requirements and the Council's approved
financial framework. The approval of carry-forward budgets is
necessary where schemes remain approved, committed or otherwise
required to continue into 2026/27.
 
The recommendations also respond to the wider
delivery pattern within the programme. The outturn position
indicates that a significant proportion of the approved budget has
not been spent in the year in which it was profiled. Approving
carry-forward allows necessary schemes to continue, but the report
also recognises that the Council needs stronger management
information to distinguish between expected multi-year delivery and
avoidable slippage. The revised delivery classification analysis is
intended to support that improvement.
 
The analysis in this report groups schemes by
delivery characteristics. This distinction matters because
carry-forward on a major multi-year project, or on a scheme
dependent on government grant conditions, planning consent, school
delivery timetables or partner-led activity, has a different
implication from carry-forward on an approved scheme that has not
progressed beyond feasibility or initial review.
 

Cabinet could decide not to approve some or
all of the carry-forward requests. This
option is not recommended where schemes are committed, legally or
contractually required, grant-funded, part of an approved
multi-year programme or required to meet Council priorities. In
those circumstances refusing such carry-forwards would risk stopping schemes that
remain valid and may create financial, operational or reputational
consequences.
 
A more selective approach to carry-forward
could be appropriate where schemes are no longer aligned with
Council priorities, remain at an early feasibility stage without a
clear delivery route, or have not demonstrated sufficient progress.
The report therefore recommends approval of the overall
carry-forward position while also highlighting the need for
continued review of schemes with limited or no in-year delivery.
This gives Cabinet assurance that carry-forward is not being
treated as automatic, but as part of a more disciplined capital
programme management process.
 

None.

content:
To present an
updated Section 75 (S75) agreement of the NHS Act 2006 to the
Executive Director: People and Cabinet Member for Adults, Economy
and Regeneration for review and approval.
To inform the
Executive Director: People and Cabinet Member for Adults, Economy
and Regeneration of the changes made to the previous S75 in
consultation with legal services.
 

RESOLVED that the
Executive Director: People in consultation with the Cabinet
Member for Adults, Economy and Regeneration to approve that BFC agrees and enters
into a S75 agreement with Thames Valley Integrated Care
Board (ICB) from 1 April 2026 effective for a period of up to two
years (1 + 1).
 

The previous S75 Agreement
expired 31 March 2026. Existing and new services that are jointly
commissioned and/or funded through a pooled budget need to be
covered through a S75 Agreement in order to be compliant with the
NHS Act 2006 and have a clear working protocol between Thames
Valley ICB and Bracknell Forest Council.
 
The previous S75 agreement was
entered into between Frimley ICB and Bracknell Forest Council. On 1
April 2026, Frimley ICB ceased to exist as an entity and Bracknell
Forest is now part of the Thames Valley ICB footprint.
 
In light of this change, it is
recognised that 2026-2027 is a transition year and it is therefore
proposed that a 1 + 1 agreement (allowing for a 1-year
extension)  would be most appropriate.
The Better Care Fund (BCF) guidance stipulates that S75 agreements
need to be in place by 30th September each year, so many
Health and Wellbeing Boards have S75 agreements that run October
– September. It is acknowledged that there may be an
intention to align agreement dates across the Thames Valley
footprint. Opting for a 1 + 1 term allows the agreement to be
finalised under existing terms and conditions, and then to be
reviewed prior to March 2027.
 
The S75 agreement encompasses
three schedules: one pertaining to the Better Care Fund; one
pertaining to Heathlands Care Home; and a third schedule that was
added as a deed of variation during 25-26 is a schedule pertaining
to Bridgewell. This is therefore a key
strategic document governing ways of working between Bracknell
Forest Council and Thames Valley ICB. The schedules are updated and
mutually agreed on an annual basis, in line with any new
guidance.
 
The scheme of delegation
reflects approval for S75 by the Executive Director: People in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Adults, Economy and
Regeneration.
 
The S75 agreement will progress through Thames
Valley ICB’s governance route in tandem with the
Council’s governance process.
 

Other options such as extending the existing
S75 Agreement or not renewing the S75 Agreement are not feasible
options as would lead us to be non-compliant.
 
A longer term agreement has been considered,
but due to the period of transition, a shorter-term agreement was
deemed to be most appropriate.
 

None.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Health
purpose:
To approve the Education Transport Framework
award decision.
content:
RESOLVED that the Cabinet Member for
Children, Young People and Health approve the contract award of the
Education Transport Framework ahead of its commencement on 1st
August 2026.
 
The Executive Director: People, in
consultation with the Executive Member for Children, Young People
and Health, be authorised to exercise the options to extend the
framework contract for the additional three year and two year
periods under delegated authority.
 

In accordance with BFC contract standing
orders, the decision to approve the contract award is delegated to
the Cabinet Member: Children, Young People and Health.
 
Bids were reviewed by the Framework Tender
Evaluation team and only bids which met the requirements of the
specification were accepted onto the framework.
 
Local authorities in England have statutory
duties in relation to education transport under the Education Act
1996 and associated statutory guidance. Their core responsibility
is to make suitable and free transport arrangements where these are
necessary to enable eligible children of compulsory school age to
attend school.
 

Do nothing, let existing Dynamic Purchasing
System (DPS) lapse - If no action is taken and the current DPS and
associated contracts would lapse leading to a significant failure
in the Council meeting its statutory duties. This would lead to
significant challenges from parents and carers, as well as
increased pressure on other Council services.
 
Re-commission using a Dynamic Market – a
Dynamic Market allows for new providers to join at any time which
is resource intensive and may result in reduced quality assurance
and monitoring. Under a Dynamic Market arrangement, it is not
permissible to issue below-threshold call-off contracts. This
restriction would not be suitable for this service, given the
operational requirement to award contracts of varying values,
including those that may fall below the relevant procurement
thresholds.
 
Spot purchase transport provision - Best value
for money is unlikely to be achieved. This may result in reduced
quality assurance and monitoring. This may also cause delays in
delivering essential services for Children & Young People and
their families.
 

None.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Health has decided to approve the contract award for the Education Transport Framework.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Health
purpose:
To approve the commissioning of Provision of
Education and Transport for Children and Young People Following
Permanent Exclusion including a cohort with Education Health Care
Plans award decision
content:
That the Executive Director of People/Cabinet
Member:Children, Young People and
Health approves the contract award, commencing on 1 August 2026, to
Provider A for an initial period of two years, with the option of
one further one-year extension to a maximum of three years (2+1
years) subject to satisfactory performance

To complete the procurement process for a
provider of education and associated transport for children and
young people who have been permanently excluded from mainstream
education, including a cohort with Education, Health and Care Plans
(EHCPs).
 
Evaluation of the quality and pricing, and
subsequent moderation process the Most Advantageous Tender was
offered by Provider A and as such is recommended for award of
contract subject to approvals. The quality responses within the
tender submission were consistently strong, demonstrating a high
level of assurance that the bidder understands the requirements and
can deliver a safe, high-quality service. The submission also
achieved the full 5% weighting for social value, reflecting a clear
and well-evidenced commitment to delivering additional benefits
beyond core service requirements.
 
The anticipated benefits delivered through
awarding the contract to Provider A will include:
·      
Commissioning this service will ensure continuity of education and
transport for excluded pupils
·      
Ensuring continuing compliance with legislation and statutory
duties
·      
Ensuring good quality and value for money education services which
focus on meeting the needs of permanently excluded children and
young people and achieving positive outcomes.
 

Do nothing: The Council would be unable
to meet its statutory duty to provide education for permanently
excluded pupils.
 
Spot purchase education placements or
packages as and when required: Places in other Local Authority
PRUs are in high demand so there will be no guarantee of places
available if these are spot purchased. Bespoke packages from the
unregulated market are likely to be much higher in cost if spot
purchased, and so better value for money would be achieved by block
purchasing.
 
Extend existing contract: Extending the
existing contract would not be in line with procurement laws, which
requires a formal competitive process to take place for a contract
of this value.
 

None.

purpose:
To seek the formal adoption of the Parking
Standards Supplementary Planning Document 202 to be used as a
material consideration in the determination of relevant planning
applications
content:
RESOLVED That the Cabinet:
i. Approves the adoption of the Parking
Standards Supplementary Planning
Document (2026) (Appendix A).
ii. Approves that the existing Parking
Standards Supplementary Planning
Document (2016) is withdrawn.
iii. Delegates authority to the Executive
Director: Place in consultation with
the Cabinet Member for Planning, Transport and
Countryside to approve
any necessary minor amendments to the Parking
Standards
Supplementary Planning Document (2026) prior
to publication.

Planning applications are being determined in
accordance with Local Plan policies as detailed in paragraph 1.2
above.  It is important that up-to-date
associated guidance is made available to provide prospective
applicants with a clearer understanding of the Council’s
requirements regarding policies concerned with parking standards
and associated parking matters.
 
Once adopted it will replace the existing
Parking Standards SPD which was adopted in 2016.
 
]The current Parking Standards Supplementary
Planning Document dated 2016 is increasingly out-of-date. It refers
to the old Use Classes Order and fails to provide parking standards
to serve developments such as large Houses in Multiple Occupation
(HMOs) and Suitable Alternative Natural Greenspaces (SANGs). It
also adopts an inflexible approach which does not support the
Council’s  strategy to focus new
development in and around the town centre and encourage the use of
sustainable transport options.
 
 
The Parking Standards Supplementary Planning
Document 2026 addresses these issues, including by
introducing  a more flexible approach to
parking provision in instances where this can be robustly justified
and supported through the provision of sustainable transport
options such as car clubs and financial contributions toward
off-site travel planning measures.
 
The preparation of the SPD contributes towards
the Council Plan (2023-2027) priorities by ensuring that Bracknell
town centre continues to thrive, the local transport network
provides choice in travel and there is collective action to address
and adapt to the climate emergency.
 

The Council could opt to not produce an SPD
and instead rely on the current out-of-date and incorrect SPD dated
2016.  The absence of an adopted up to
date SPD would make the assessment of planning applications open to
interpretation and inconsistent with national regulations.
Production of the SPD will assist potential developers and other
interested parties by providing clarity on the Council’s
expectations in how parking provision to serve new developments
should be provided.
 
There is no option to delay the
adoption of the SPD.  This is because
Regulation 6 (of Schedule 1) of the Levelling-up and Regeneration
Act 2023 (Commencement No.11 and Saving and Transitional
Provisions) Regulations 2026 states that supplementary planning
documents can be adopted no later than 30 June 2026.  This is part of the changes to the national plan
making system.
 

None.

purpose:
To approve the Strategic Procurement Plan for
Short Breaks for Children and Young People with
Disabilities
content:
RESOLVED that the Cabinet:
 

·      
Approves the Strategic Procurement Plan for the procurement of
Targeted Short Breaks Services.

·      
Approve the proposed contractual term of five years starting with
an initial period of wo years, with the option to extend for
further three years (2+3 years).

·      
Notes the following model for Targeted Short Breaks Services:
o  
Recommission a new Targeted Short Breaks Play Scheme with 5-hour
sessions in line with the Strategic Procurement Plan.
o  
 Commission separate short-term services
via Request for Quotation. Short term services will be delivered as
activity-based sessions and will target children and young people
with mild to moderate special educational needs and disabilities
(SEND) / social emotional mental health (SEMH) needs who are not
eligible for Inclusion Fund support and do not meet the threshold
for the Targeted Short Breaks Play Scheme.
o  
Continue with supporting children and young people through the
inclusion fund.
 
 

·      
 Delegate authority to the Executive
Director: People in consultation with Portfolio Lead for Children
Young People & Health to approve contract award and permitted
contract extensions. 
 

Local Authorities have statutory duties to
provide short breaks for children with     disabilities and
their families, in line with the Children’s Act 1989 and
Breaks for Carers of Disabled Children Regulations
2011.  In performing their duties under
paragraph 6(1)(c) of Schedule 2 to the 1989 Act, Local Authorities
must provide, so far as is reasonably practicable, a range of
services which is sufficient to assist carers to continue to
provide care or to do so more effectively. In particular, the Local
Authority must provide, as appropriate, a range of:
·      
Day-time care in the homes of disabled children or elsewhere,
·      
Overnight care in the homes of disabled children or elsewhere,
·      
Educational or leisure activities for disabled children outside
their homes and
·      
Services available to assist carers in the evenings, at weekends
and during school holidays.
 
To provide sufficient capacity to meet current
and increasing demand, in line with the increase of children and
young people with an education health & care plan.
 
This is a long running provision that has been
instrumental in raising the participation of children and young
people with disabilities in rewarding activities and supports
inclusion in the local community and supports the priorities within
the Children Social Care Service Plan.
 
The use of an Invitation to Tender (ITT)
provides a transparent and competitive route to market, allowing
the Council to identify, assess, and select the most suitable
providers while achieving value for money and ensuring service
quality.
 
Proceeding with a formal procurement process
will ensure full compliance with the Public Procurement Act 2023
and Bracknell Forest Council’s Contract Standing Orders.
Approval is required to support the timely completion of tendering,
award, and mobilisation activities, enabling the contract to
commence as planned in April 2027.
 
The proposed procurement of this service
through a single stage tender will help maximise tender
opportunities that should generate value for money and high-quality
Short Breaks provision. The inclusion of multiple lots enables
potentially more than one provider to deliver the service.
 
The proposed option will enable commissioning
of additional short?term services to support families who do not
currently access provision and look to expand provision to support
more children and young people. Additional short-term services will
be commissioned in accordance with Contract Standing Orders.
 
Parents and carers expressed clear support for
the proposed delivery model, including the agreed session length,
and shared the importance of maintaining flexibility across age
groups, levels of need, and types of provision. In addition,
families supported a blended approach that incorporates shorter,
regular, and predictable sessions, alongside stay?and?play
opportunities for younger children.
 

Recommission a new Short Breaks service
with 3-hour sessions - The model proposes shorter session
durations, from six hours to three hours, with an increased number
of sessions available, reflecting feedback received from parents
and carers during the first consultation. However, this proposal is
acknowledged to be contrary to views expressed by parents and
carers during the second consultation. This equates to a similar
total number of hours to the current service offer; however,
support would be delivered through shorter, more frequent sessions.
This option would not allow for additional services to be
commissioned within the existing budget to support families not
currently accessing provision.
 
Recommission a Short Breaks service with
6-hour sessions - Maintaining the current session length would
limit opportunities to develop or expand the Short Breaks service.
This option would not allow for additional services to be
commissioned within the existing budget to support families not
currently accessing provision.
 
Recommission existing service and keep
things as they are - The existing service is operating at full
capacity and has already required significant contract variations
and additional investment to maintain service delivery. The current
model is not sustainable, as the number of children accommodated
per session is no longer viable given the increasingly complex
needs of the young people supported. Without the commissioning of
different targeted services and the establishment of a clear
pathway underpinned by transparent and well-defined eligibility
criteria, there is a significant risk that the Short Breaks Service
will be unable to meet the growing level of need within the
Borough.
 
Extending - Extending the existing
arrangements is not possible, the current service is already at
capacity and has required significant contract variation and
additional investment to sustain services. The current model is not
sustainable.
 
Do nothing and the current contract ceases
on 31st March 2027 - Current contractual obligation will lapse;
there would be no adequate provision to meet our statutory duties
or meet the commitments in line with the Local Area SEND Inspection
and SEND Improvement Plan. This will see significant challenge from
parents / carers and increase pressures on other services.
 
Spot Purchasing without a contractual
agreement - Best value for money is unlikely to be achieved.
Spot Purchases would not attract the same speed of response as
referrals made under contract. This would not support forward
planning for this service.
 
Bring Service In-House - Due to the
timescales and resource available, a full exploration of in-house
services could not be explored at this time. There are lots of
factors to consider if the service were to be brought in-house,
including potential costs, staffing, the management of the service
and potential venues.

Biodiversity and Green Infrastructure Supplementary Planning

The Bracknell Forest Local Plan was adopted in
March 2024 and sets out the vision and strategy for the Borough to
2037.

now being determined in accordance with the Bracknell Forest Local
Plan, which contains the strategic policies LP 30 Green
Infrastructure, LP 31 Designated nature conservation and geological
sites and policy LP 53 Biodiversity. It is important that
associated guidance is provided to avoid ambiguity about how
policies will be interpreted and applied in the determination of
planning applications.

policies should be applied. In providing clarity, the Council is
less likely to be put into an appeal position with a need to defend
policies on these matters (reducing the financial and time burden

making system.

The recommendations in this report can be

content:
To procure an Omni-Channel Customer Contact
Platform to support Customer Contact Centre using services
such as phone, email, web chat, SMS, social media that can route,
track and record interactions supporting agents with appropriate
tools, scripts and knowledge

RESOLVED that the Cabinet:
 

·      
approves the procurement of the Council’s Omni-Channel
Customer Contact Platform via direct award under the NHS SBS10521
– Patient / Citizen Communication, Engagement & Hybrid
Mail Solutions Framework, lot 3;

·      
delegates authority to the Executive Director: Resources, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Leisure, Culture, Public
Protection, to award the contract for the services outlined in
3.1.
 

The platform underpins the Council’s
customer contact centre and the management   of resident enquiries across telephony and digital
channels. Renewing it is necessary   to
keep services running, maintain resident access to key services and
ensure          
ongoing legal and licensing compliance.
 
The platform is already embedded within the
Council’s operating model and is tightly integrated with
other systems, including our configurable low-code platform.
Replacing it would require significant redesign, re-integration,
staff retraining and transition activity, creating additional cost,
disruption and risk without sufficient benefit at this stage.
 
 
The recommended route is a direct award under
the NHS SBS10521 – Patient / Citizen Communication,
Engagement & Hybrid Mail Solutions Framework, lot 3. This is
considered a lawful and proportionate route that supports service
continuity and avoids            
the disruption and cost of a full procurement exercise for a
platform the Council already relies on heavily.
 
Alternative routes and framework options were
considered, but none was assessed as offering a more proportionate
combination of compliance, operational fit, value for money and
risk. The recommended route is therefore considered to provide the
most appropriate basis for securing continuity of service and
contractual compliance at this time.
 
 

Alternative customer contact and omni-channel
platforms were considered in principle. However, moving to a
different system would require major replacement activity,
re-integration with back-office workflows and case management
processes, retraining of staff and transition planning. This would
involve significant cost and risk without enough added benefit to
justify changing platform at this stage.
 
 Alternative
procurement routes, including other available frameworks such as
CCS G-Cloud 14 (RM1557.14) and CCS RM6285, were also reviewed.
These were not preferred because they did not offer as strong a fit
with the Council’s requirements, nor a more proportionate or
lower-risk route for this requirement.

purpose:
To procure a configurable environment to build
and manage online forms, automate and run end-to-end business
processes (workflows), and deliver case management, with
integrations to key third-party system.
content:
RESOLVED that the Cabinet;
 
·      
approves the procurement of the Council’s configurable
low-code platform through a direct award under the NHS SBS10521
Patient / Citizen Communication, Engagement & Hybrid Mail
Solutions Framework, Lot 3 and
·      
delegates authority to the Executive Director: Resources, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Leisure, Culture, Public
Protection, to award the contract for the services outlined in
3.1.
 

This platform is essential to the
Council’s day-to-day delivery of online services, internal
workflows and case handling across a range of high-volume services.
It supports a significant part of the Council’s digital
service infrastructure, including online forms, resident
self-service through My Account, and the routing and management of
service requests through to completion. Renewing it is necessary to
maintain service continuity, resident access to key services and
ongoing licensing compliance. It also supports the Council’s
wider ambition to provide residents with accessible, connected and
responsive services through a more consistent digital offer.
 
The platform is already embedded in the
Council’s operating model and integrated with customer
contact systems and other core software. Replacing it would require
services to be redesigned, integrations to be rebuilt, staff to be
retrained and a major transition to be managed, creating additional
cost, disruption and delivery risk.
 
The recommended route is a direct award under
the NHS SBS10521 Patient / Citizen Communication, Engagement &
Hybrid Mail Solutions Framework. This is considered a lawful and
proportionate route that supports service continuity and avoids the
cost, disruption and implementation risk of a full procurement
exercise fora platform on which the Council already relies.
 
Alternative routes and framework options were
considered, but none was assessed as offering a more proportionate
combination of compliance, operational fit, value for money and
risk. The recommended route is therefore considered to provide the
most appropriate basis for securing continuity of service and
contractual compliance at this time.
 

Other digital workflow and case management
systems were considered in principle. However, moving to a
different platform would require substantial redevelopment of the
Council’s existing online forms, workflows, integrations and
service processes. This would involve significant cost and risk
without sufficient additional benefit to justify a change at this
stage.
 
Alternative procurement routes, including use
of other available frameworks such as CCS G-Cloud 14 and CCS
RM6285, were also reviewed. These were not preferred because they
did not offer as strong a fit with the Council’s
requirements, timing and existing delivery model, or a more
proportionate route for this procurement.

purpose:

secure a framework for capital programme works and other property

content:
RESOLVED That
the Cabinet:
 

·      
Approves the Strategic Procurement Plan in
confidential Appendix A.

·      
Delegates authority to the Executive Director of
Place, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Adults, Economy
and Regeneration, to

re-award the Capital Works Framework to new suppliers when there

o  
approve project call?offs in accordance with the
framework terms and Council governance arrangements via its
contract standing orders.
 
 

The Council must maintain the ability to
deliver its capital programme in a safe, compliant and timely
manner across its estate and public realm, in accordance with
statutory, contractual and governance obligations.
 
 The Strategic
Procurement Plan sets out how the proposed Capital Works Framework
will meet the Council’s value for money and transparency
objectives through a compliant competitive procurement process and
a strengthened commercial model, providing improved cost certainty
and assurance.
 
 The establishment
of a framework will ensure service continuity and consistent
quality by providing access to a pre?qualified supply chain,
reducing procurement lead?in times and enabling earlier contractor
engagement on individual projects.
 
The framework will support improved risk
management and delivery performance by standardising contract
terms, performance management arrangements, and reporting
requirements across capital projects.
 
The Council seeks to maximise diversity and
inclusion, sustainability and social value outcomes through its
procurement activity. The framework specification embeds
requirements relating to:
 

carbon reduction and sustainable
construction practices;
efficient use of resources and
whole?life cost considerations;
delivery of measurable social value,
including apprenticeships, local employment, and supply?chain
opportunities for Small and Medium Enterprises and Voluntary,
Community and Social Enterprises; and
engagement with local communities
and alignment with wider Council priorities.

 

The cabinet could decide:

the recommendations to cabinet as set out in the panel’s
report,
 • to endorse
the recommendations in part,
• to suggest that further work be
undertaken recognising that this would delay the panel’s next
piece of work,

purpose:
To formally approve the Local Area SEND Reform
Plan. This follows submission to the DfE on 19 June as per the
delegated authority to Executive Director People in consultation
with the Cabinet Member for Children Young People and Health,
agreed by Cabinet on 28 April
content:
RESOLVED that the Cabinet
 

·      
Endorses the final Local SEND Reform Plan 2026–2029 and Local
Partnership  Maturity Matrix, noting
that the plan will already have been submitted to the Department
for Education on 19 June 2026 in line with national timelines and
agreedat the 28 April 2026 Cabinet meeting.
 

·      
Delegates authority to the Executive Director: People, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and
Health, to agree the Experts at Hand grant expenditure in line with
national grant conditions to mobilise the offer / service by
September 2026
 

The Local SEND Reform Plan is the national
accountability vehicle through which Government will assess the
readiness and credibility of local area partnerships’ SEND
reform approaches. Local areas are required to submit plans to the
Department for Education to secure approval and access associated
national support and funding arrangements.
 
Approval of the final plan provides
Cabinet-level confirmation of the partnership’s strategic
direction and local commitment. Although the plan will already have
been submitted under delegated authority in line with national
timelines, Cabinet endorsement is important for transparent
democratic oversight and reinforces collective accountability for
delivery across education, health and care.
 
Cabinet is also asked to agree delegation for
decisions and spend relating to the Experts at Hand grant. This
grant is intended to fund the development and delivery of a new
Experts at Hand offer for mainstream settings and to fund necessary
local authority administrative and transformation activity linked
to SEND reform planning.
 
Mobilisation timescales are challenging.
Decisions will be required at pace over the summer period to ensure
that services, workforce arrangements and delivery mechanisms are
operational for September. Returning to Cabinet for subsequent
approvals for individual spend decisions would create a significant
risk of delay and would undermine the ability to meet expected
national timelines and local delivery requirements. Delegation to
the Executive Director: People, in consultation with the relevant
Cabinet Member, provides the necessary agility while retaining
appropriate accountability and governance.
 

No alternative options were considered. The
local area partnership is required to develop and submit a Local
SEND Reform Plan in June 2026, underpinned by a Local Partnership
Maturity Assessment, in line with the nationally prescribed
framework and commissioning arrangements.

None

purpose:
To seek approval
for the commitment of £31,866.60 S106 to the Buckler’s

content:
To seek approval
for the commitment of £31,866.60 S106 to the Buckler’s
Park Community Hub kitchenette project.

RESOLVED:
 
 That approval is
given for expenditure of £31,866.60 from S106 contributions
on the Buckler’s Park Community Hub for installation of a
kitchenette to serve users of the hall and meeting rooms. The
proposals will be funded through S106 Agreement developer
contributions totalling £31,866.60 specifically from:
13/00575/OUT - Transport Research Laboratory
(TRL), Crowthorne - YN564
(On completion of the First Deed of Variation
to pay to the Council the sum of £150,000 by way of
contribution towards the costs of temporary primary school
accommodation and school transport costs and or the cost of works
on the Community Hub or the on-going maintenance of the Community
Hub or Community Hub Land. Amount left to spend:
£31,866.60).
2.2 Bracknell Forest Council (BFC) to take
full responsibility for delivering the improvement works to the
community hub. This will include obtaining competitive quotations,
liaising directly with contractors, managing the procurement
process, and overseeing all aspects of the installation to ensure
the project is completed to a high standard, on time, and within
budget.
2.3 BFC to provide regular progress updates
and a final completion report to Age Concern Bracknell Forest who
manage the hub, ensuring transparency and accountability throughout
the project.

 
 3.1 The proposed
works includes the installation of a new basic fitted kitchen to
enhance the range of services available to centre users, utilising
an existing storage area within the main hall that has been
identified as an appropriate location due to its established access
to essential utilities. Suitable alternative storage for users is
available elsewhere on site. This will incorporate:
 

•               
Cabinets to provide storage of equipment

•               
Food storage and preparation areas

•               
Dish and hand-washing facilities

•               
Appropriate hygiene signage
 

 
 4.1 Bracknell
Forest Council to fully project manage
 
Bracknell Forest Council to take full
responsibility for delivering the kitchen refurbishment, including
scoping, procurement, contractor coordination, and budget
management. This provides professional expertise and reduces the
workload on the community centre, offering a single point of
contact. The BFC Property Team bring substantial professional
expertise and a proven track record in managing complex property
matters, ensuring the project is supported by knowledgeable and
experienced specialists. A project management fee of 15% will
apply.
 
4.2 Community Hub Funding
 
The Community Hub has not yet generated
sufficient surplus to contribute towards the cost of the kitchen
refurbishment. While the hub continues to build its income streams
and strengthen its financial position, it is currently unable to
allocate the funds required for this project.
 
4.3 Bracknell Forest Council Funding
 
Due to existing budget pressures, Bracknell
Forest Council is unable to provide financial assistance for this
work through the Capital programme. Consequently, committing S106
funding is critical to enabling these improvements. Securing this
support will ensure that the community continues to benefit from
accessible, high-quality spaces that foster engagement, wellbeing,
and resilience and will ensure the building remains fit for purpose
in the long term.
 
4.4 External Funding
 
Securing grant funding for Age Concern
Bracknell Forest is challenging, as many funding streams do not
support the refurbishment of existing facilities. Most grant
providers prioritise new initiatives, programme delivery, or
community-focused activities, which means opportunities to fund
essential building upgrades are limited. As a result, identifying
suitable external funding for the kitchen refurbishment has proven
difficult.
 
4.5 Allocation of s106 funding is not
approved
 
Without this funding, the kitchen
refurbishment will not be able to proceed. This will prevent the
centre from offering a much-needed facility for the community, and
it will have a direct impact on party and event bookings, which
currently provide a valuable source of income. As there is
currently no kitchen facility for hirers it will make it
increasingly difficult to meet hirers’ expectations. Without
improvements, the centre risks losing bookings, reducing revenue
and limiting its ability to sustain wider community activities and
services.

N/A

purpose:
To consider a request from the taxi trade to
amend the Hackney Carriage Fare Chart following the consultation
period.
content:
RESOLVED that the Cabinet:

·      
Notes the objection received during the statutory consultation

·      
Agrees the table of fares at Appendix A, with an implementation
date of the 29 May 2026.

Local authorities have a
statutory power to set the maximum fares that licensed hackney
carriages (taxis) can charge for a journey.  Under section 65 of the Local Government
(Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976, local authorities have the
power to “…fix the rates or fares within the district
as well for time as distance, and all other charges in connection
with the hire of a vehicle or with the arrangements for the hire of
a vehicle, to be paid in respect of the hire of hackney carriages
by means of a table (hereafter in this section referred to as a
“table of fares”) made or varied in accordance with the
provisions of this section.” The Act also sets out the
statutory process for conducting a consultation should the local
authority consider making any changes to the tariffs.
 
The taxi trade submitted a
business case asking for two changes to be made to the existing
fare chart. The first change sought to increase the existing
fouling charges from £50 (internal fouling) and £10
(external fouling) to £80 (internal fouling) and £25
(external fouling). The trade stated that these charges were
proposed to reflect that valeting and car wash costs have increased
over the years.
 
The second requested change was
a presentational change in relation to journeys when vehicles are
carrying five or more passengers. The current fare chart states
“When this vehicle is carrying more than 4 passengers, a
surcharge of 50% will be applied to the fare shown on the meter at
the end of the journey.  This will however not be shown on the taximeter.”
The trade have reported that this causes confusion
for passengers and that they would prefer to show the information
as stated on Appendix A and for the fares to be programmed into the
meters.
 
A consultation was undertaken
and three responses were received including one objection to the
proposals. As an objection to the varied
table of fares has been received and not withdrawn the matter must
be considered by the Cabinet who must decide whether or not to
modify the table of fares before it comes into effect and to set a
further date for the table to come into effect.
 
 

The
options, in accordance with the statutory framework, are set out
below.
 

None.

purpose:

Community Centre refurbishment.
content:
RESOLVED  That
approval is given for expenditure of £20,000 from S106
contributions on the Easthampstead and Wildridings Community Centre
for refurbishment of the existing kitchen facilities. The proposals
will be funded through s106 Agreement developer contributions
totalling £20,000 specifically from:

•               
13/00296/FUL Broughs, Broad Lane YN540 = £952

•               
12/00492/EXT Land adj Birch Hill Medical Centre YN534 =
£4,475

•               
13/01036/FUL 22 Bennings Close YN502 = £50

•               
07/01259/FUL Land at Brakenhale School YN372 = £14,523
 
Easthampstead and Wildridings Community
Association (EWCA) to take full responsibility for delivering the
improvement works to the community centre. This will include
obtaining competitive quotations, liaising directly with
contractors, managing the procurement process, and overseeing all
aspects of the refurbishment to ensure the project is completed to
a high standard, on time, and within budget.
 
Bracknell Forest Council’s Corporate
Property Team shall provide overall project oversight, ensuring
adherence to all compliance requirements and maintaining
transparent governance arrangements. The team will also offer
professional guidance and support throughout the duration of the
project. A management fee equivalent to 5% of the total project
cost shall be applied.
 
EWCA to provide regular progress updates and a
final completion report to Bracknell Forest Council, ensuring
transparency and accountability throughout the project

 
To seek approval to undertake capacity
improvements to the community centre facilities. The proposed works
include installation of a new fitted kitchen to enhance the range
of services available to centre users. This will incorporate:

•               
Cooking facilities

•               
Washing facilities

•               
Refrigeration units

•               
General storage solutions.
 
 To further enhance
the space, refurbishment works will be required, including:

•               
Replacement of flooring

•               
Replastering of visible walls

•               
General redecoration of the area
 
Additional requirements will include
procurement of complementary equipment to support the upgraded
kitchen facilities, such as:

•               
Microwave oven

•               
Refreshment-making equipment.
 

Allocation of s106
is not approved.
If s106 is not approved, the kitchen
refurbishment cannot proceed. Easthampstead & Wildridings
Community Association will then face significant limitations in its
ability to support residents and deliver vital community services.
The existing kitchen facilities are no longer fit to meet current
and future demand, restricting the range, scale, and quality of
activities that can be offered.
 
 External
funding
As the building is owned by Bracknell Forest
Council, EWCA is not eligible to apply for many external grants,
which typically require applicants to hold the freehold or a
long-term lease.
 
 Bracknell Forest
Council Funding

Forest Council is unable to provide financial assistance for this

improvements. Securing this support will ensure that the community
continues to benefit from accessible, high-quality spaces that

None.

purpose:
To seek approval for the Strategic Procurement
Plan for the Provision of Education and Transport for Children and
Young People Following Permanent Exclusion including a cohort with
Education Health Care Plans. The current contract expires on 31st
July 2026, and new arrangements need to be in place by 1st
September 2026. To seek approval for delegated authority to the
